page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c16g1.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the Compute Optimized with GPU family. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4 GB of memory per core. For hardware acceleration, it integrates a single NVIDIA P4 graphics processing unit equipped with 8 GB of VRAM.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance does not include local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of network-backed block storage for operational volumes and persistent data handling.

From a resource and cost efficiency perspective, pairing 16 vCPUs and a mid-tier NVIDIA P4 GPU allows organizations to provision dedicated accelerator capabilities without the overhead of massive multi-GPU configurations. The 8 GB GPU memory ceiling and reliance on remote storage serve as key tradeoffs to factor into system architecture design.

The ecs.gn5i-c16g1.4xlarge instance is suited for GPU-accelerated computing jobs, small-to-medium scale machine learning inference, computer vision processing, video transcoding pipelines, and general GPU-assisted enterprise applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c16g1.4xlarge is a dedicated GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for compute and inference tasks. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64 GB of memory, yielding a 4 GB per core allocation. Hardware acceleration is delivered by an integrated NVIDIA P4 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Networking includes a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included by default. The platform provisions zero local block storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for all OS installations and data persistence. Combining 16 host cores with entry-to-mid-range accelerator hardware makes this server a practical choice for machine learning inference, media encoding, image processing pipelines, and data processing workflows that require hardware acceleration without high accelerator density.
